plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1914 & Summer 1944–1946 (Karl von Frisch in Munich and Brunnwinkl proves honeybees see colour and ultraviolet light, then uses paint-numbered bees in a glass hive to decode the figure-eight waggle dance sun-to-gravity code) · 1949 & 1951–1955 (Karl von Frisch discovers the bee's ultraviolet polarized-sky compass, and Martin Lindauer discovers time-compensated marathon dances and swarm house-hunting democracy) · June 1989 (Axel Michelsen, Wolfgang Kirchner, and Martin Lindauer build a computer-controlled brass-and-wax mechanical robot bee pulsing at 280 Hz that sends real honeybees to programmed field targets).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1914 → 1989) alongside an inked summary of honeybee colour vision, the sun-to-gravity waggle code, polarized-sky navigation, swarm democracy, and the 1989 mechanical robot bee
teach_overlay.scale: from five dots of shellac paint on an Austrian lakeside to a vibrating razor-blade robot in a dark hive, scientists proved that the smallest brains in your garden speak a mathematical language of the Sun
